rationale: C16 plausibly supplied a material template for the child: both establish an ordered departmental succession to the duties of a cabinet secretary upon the absence, sickness, resignation, or death of the Secretary and Under Secretary, then identify the next eligible officer and conclude with a supersession clause. The child adapts that machinery by separating the succession into subparagraphs and defining which Assistant Secretary ranks first. C11 and C15 use closely related Post Office succession language, but C16 is the stronger departmental and structural analogue.

shared_material.child_excerpt: in case of the death, resignation, absence, or sickness of both the Secretary of the Interior and the Under Secretary of the Interior
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In case of the absence, sickness, resignation, or death of both the Secretary of Agriculture and the Under Secretary of Agriculture
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively close contingency language applied to the same Secretary–Under Secretary succession relationship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The ranking Assistant Secretary of the Interior present shall perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the officer whose name is highest on the following list and who is not absent or under disability to discharge the duties of the office of the Secretary of Agriculture shall perform the duties of that office
shared_material.explanation: Both designate the highest-ranking available subordinate to perform a department secretary's duties.
Parallel closing provision replacing an earlier departmental succession directive.
